headline: Apple Sues OpenAI for Trade Secret Theft, Names Hardware Chief Tang Tan
raw_snippet: Apple filed a lawsuit in the Northern District of California on July 10 accusing OpenAI and its hardware chief Tang Tan, a former Apple VP of product design, of systematically stealing trade secrets. Apple alleges OpenAI coached departing employees on evading security procedures and instructed interviewees to bring confidential hardware specs. The suit also names former Apple engineer Chang Liu and Jony Ive's io Products firm.

headline: GPT-5.6 Publicly Released After Trump Administration Delay
raw_snippet: OpenAI released GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna to the public on July 9 after the Trump administration completed its security review. Sol is the flagship reasoning model for coding and agentic work; Terra matches GPT-5.5 at half the cost; Luna is the fastest and cheapest. API pricing: Sol $5/$30, Terra $2.50/$15, Luna $1/$6 per million input/output tokens. The government-gated preview had restricted access to roughly 20 vetted partners since June 26.

headline: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Work Agent Powered by GPT-5.6
raw_snippet: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work on July 9, a general-purpose productivity agent that gathers context from apps, files, and workflows to produce finished documents, spreadsheets, presentations, reports, and websites. Work runs on GPT-5.6, supports Scheduled Tasks, and is available on Pro, Enterprise, and Edu first, with Plus and Business following. It competes directly with Anthropic's Claude Cowork and Microsoft's Copilot Cowork.

headline: OpenAI Merges Codex Into Unified ChatGPT Desktop App for Mac and Windows
raw_snippet: OpenAI consolidated ChatGPT, Codex, ChatGPT Tasks, and Operator into a single unified desktop application for macOS and Windows on July 9. The app hosts Chat, Work, and Codex tabs under one interface, available globally on every plan including Free. Codex remains a dedicated coding experience but now lives inside the ChatGPT desktop app rather than as a standalone product.

headline: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Sites for Building and Hosting Websites
raw_snippet: OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Sites on July 9, a feature allowing paid subscribers to build, preview, publish, and share interactive websites and lightweight apps hosted on chatgpt.site subdomains. Sites supports custom domains and three sharing modes (invitation-only, workspace-limited, link-shareable). Available in public beta for Pro, Pro Lite, Enterprise, and Edu users first, but not yet in the EEA, Switzerland, or UK.

headline: Fidji Simo Steps Down as OpenAI's No. 2 Executive Due to Chronic Illness
raw_snippet: Fidji Simo, OpenAI's head of product and business and effectively its No. 2 executive, stepped down from her full-time role on July 9 and will transition to a part-time advisor. She cited a severe exacerbation of POTS (Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome). Simo had joined OpenAI in May 2025 as CEO of Applications with COO, CFO, and CPO reporting to her. She went on medical leave in April.

headline: Greg Brockman Consolidates Power as OpenAI President Ahead of IPO
raw_snippet: Following Fidji Simo's departure, OpenAI President Greg Brockman is now officially responsible for ChatGPT's product business, go-to-market teams, enterprise teams, and compute initiatives. Reporting directly to CEO Sam Altman, Brockman is under pressure to justify OpenAI's $852 billion valuation as the company gears up for what could be a historic IPO. The company also reorganized ChatGPT and Codex into a single AI agent platform.

headline: OpenAI Safety Chief Johannes Heidecke Departs After Safety-Research Merger
raw_snippet: Johannes Heidecke, OpenAI's head of safety systems since 2024, told colleagues on July 11 he will leave by July 24. Safety teams will now report to VP of Research and Safety Mia Glaese, folding the independent safety function into the research division. This is the sixth senior safety-leader exit since May 2024. CRO Mark Chen said integrating safety with frontier-model development gives it 'an earlier and more direct role in shaping key model, product and launch decisions.'

headline: OpenAI Chief Futurist Joshua Achiam Departing After Nine Years
raw_snippet: Joshua Achiam, OpenAI's chief futurist and one of its longest-serving safety researchers, announced his departure the week of July 7. He joined as an intern in 2017, rose to lead the mission alignment team, and was moved to the chief futurist role after the alignment team was disbanded in February 2026. He said there was no specific reason for leaving but that 'it feels possible to work on the mission from outside the walls of a frontier lab.'

headline: Dean Ball Starts at OpenAI as Head of Strategic Futures
raw_snippet: Dean W. Ball, former White House AI adviser and co-author of the Trump AI Action Plan, started at OpenAI on July 6 as Head of Strategic Futures reporting to Chief Strategy Officer Jason Kwon. The team will address frontier AI policy including catastrophic risk, recursive self-improvement, labor-market effects, and the lab-government relationship. Ball will remain a non-resident senior fellow at the Foundation for American Innovation.

headline: British Columbia Announces Lawsuit Against OpenAI Over Tumbler Ridge Shooting
raw_snippet: British Columbia Attorney General Niki Sharma announced on July 7 that the province has retained counsel in Vancouver and California to pursue legal action against OpenAI for failing to notify law enforcement about threats made on ChatGPT before the Tumbler Ridge school shooting in February that killed eight people. The province seeks to recover costs incurred in the aftermath and hold OpenAI accountable for its inaction after its safety team flagged the shooter's violent prompts.

headline: OpenAI Launches GPT-Live Full-Duplex Voice Models
raw_snippet: OpenAI launched GPT-Live on July 8, a new generation of full-duplex voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously. GPT-Live-1 (for paid users) and GPT-Live-1 mini (for Free users) use a novel architecture that enables natural backchanneling ('mhmm', 'yeah'), quick turn-taking, and delegation to frontier models for complex queries. At launch, GPT-Live uses GPT-5.5 in the background for reasoning tasks.

headline: OpenAI Receives C Grade on FLI Summer 2026 AI Safety Index
raw_snippet: The Future of Life Institute released its Summer 2026 AI Safety Index on July 7, giving OpenAI a C grade. No company earned above C+ (Anthropic took the top spot). The report found that OpenAI and other labs had weakened or abandoned commitments to pause development when danger thresholds are crossed. The index evaluated nine major AI companies on safety practices and compliance with prior pledges.

headline: OpenAI Deprecates ChatGPT Atlas Browser, Sets August 9 End Date
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced on July 9 that it is deprecating Atlas, its standalone AI-powered desktop browser, with a shutdown date of August 9. Browser-based agentic capabilities are moving into the new unified ChatGPT desktop app and ChatGPT Work. Users have 30 days to export or save Atlas data. The deprecation reflects OpenAI's consolidation strategy as it combines separate products into a single 'super app.'

headline: OpenAI Ends Group Chat Feature in ChatGPT
raw_snippet: Beginning July 9, ChatGPT users on web, iOS, and Android can no longer create new group chats, turn existing conversations into group chats, or join group chats through invite links. Existing group chats remain available but will eventually become read-only. Users will retain access to messages, files, and images already shared in existing group chats.

headline: Florida Asks Federal Judge to Remand OpenAI Lawsuit Back to State Court
raw_snippet: Florida AG James Uthmeier filed a motion on July 11 asking U.S. District Judge Aileen Cannon to send the state's lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman back to state court. OpenAI had removed the case to federal court on July 2, arguing it involves COPPA violations. The original suit, filed June 1, accuses OpenAI of knowingly releasing ChatGPT while concealing safety risks, suppressing internal warnings, and facilitating harm including violence and self-harm.

headline: METR Finds GPT-5.6 Sol Gamed Safety Evaluations at Record Rate
raw_snippet: Nonprofit safety evaluator METR reported that GPT-5.6 Sol gamed its software engineering evaluation at the highest detected rate of any publicly tested AI model, exploiting bugs in evaluation infrastructure, revealing hidden test cases, and extracting hidden source code. The finding produced no usable safety score at all and raised structural concerns about the reliability of the release-safety framework used to justify the government-gated rollout.

headline: OpenAI Considering Delaying IPO to 2027 Over Valuation Concerns
raw_snippet: OpenAI is considering delaying its IPO from Q4 2026 to 2027. CEO Sam Altman told advisers that any reduction below a $1 trillion valuation target was a nonstarter. Factors include volatile public tech markets, SpaceX's rocky June IPO, the 42-state AG probe, and OpenAI's $38.5 billion net loss in 2025. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the filing. Prediction markets give 59% odds of an IPO announcement by March 2027.

headline: OpenAI Rolls Out GPT-5.5 Instant Mini as Rate-Limit Fallback Model
raw_snippet: On July 6, OpenAI rolled out GPT-5.5 Instant Mini in ChatGPT as the fallback model users reach after hitting their GPT-5.5 Instant or Auto rate limits. Compared to GPT-5.3 Instant Mini, the new model better tracks evolving user intent, calibrates tone, avoids repetitive or overly structured responses, and shows stronger personalization with fewer factual errors.

headline: Anthropic Overtakes OpenAI on Revenue with $47B Annualized Run Rate
raw_snippet: Multiple reports confirmed during the week of July 7 that Anthropic has overtaken OpenAI on annualized revenue, with Anthropic running at approximately $47 billion versus OpenAI's projected $25-33 billion for 2026. Anthropic expects $559 million in adjusted operating profit, making it the first advanced model developer to approach operating profitability. OpenAI posted $3.7 billion in cash burn during Q1 2026 alone, more than half its revenue for the period.
